fusion: #8 down GEMM + expert merge; #9 + residual add 2

variants.f8_atomic: seed out[T,H] with zeros + down GEMM with tl.atomic_add merge
variants.f8_token_major: one CTA per (token, n-block), topk summed in registers
variants.f9_atomic: seed out[T,H] with the residual + same atomic GEMM
variants.f9_token_major: token-major + residual load in the epilogue

baselines.unfused9_3kernel: unfused8 + a separate resadd kernel (primary #9 baseline)

tuning_protocol: Per regime, per side: coarse grid (SMEM- and accumulator-prefiltered; the unfused and atomic down GEMMs use the IDENTICAL generator) then a neighbourhood refine around the coarse winner. Every kernel of every chain is tuned on its own, then the chains are re-timed jointly over the top-k x top-k combinations and the best chain is reported, so a separately-tuned optimum cannot under-sell any side. The seed kernel's grid also contains a 'torch' pseudo-config (tensor.zero_() / .copy_()) so the fused side gets the vendor memset if that is faster. Token-major re-reads a full w2[e] per (token,expert) pair, so at prefill its grid is probe-shrunk (documented in the log) -- it loses there by two orders of magnitude, not by mistuning. Each regime runs in its own process for crash isolation.
retime: Final timings replayed with --retime: winning configs only, every chain timed 3x in an interleaved round-robin, min of medians kept. Applied identically to fused and unfused chains. First-pass numbers are preserved as first_pass_fused_ms / first_pass_unfused_ms. Token-major at regimes whose probe exceeded 200 ms is timed once (a single launch there is 0.25-1.5 s).
